body.note: Status:G-A Number: 1959 Name of book transcribed: GalatiansFirst folio transcribed: 79rBase text: TR1873ns (12Apr2012)Transcribed by: Bart KamphuisTranscription begun: 30 January 2013Transcription finished: 6 March 2013 Does this manuscript contain (delete and complete as appropriate): Lectionary annotations - No Initials and other enlarged letters - Yes Diples (> or >> in the margin next to certain text, indicating that text is a quotation from the Old Testament) - No Other remarks: The scribe uses colons when a word gets divided over two lines, but he does not do this consistently.He indicates where a new chapter begins.He prefers to write υιος in full instead of as a nomen sacrum.At several places (e.g. F 79r, end of transcription line 7) a ligature for αρ is used that is not reported in Faullmann or Gardthausen (F/G). Accordingly, there is a ligature for γαρ that is not reported in F/G (e.g. F 81r, middle of 3d line).One ligature for ερ (e.g. F 79v, beginning of the 9th line) looks like the first reported ligature for ερ in F, but definitely diverges from it. Another ligature for ερ, similar to the third reported ligature for ερ in F (e.g. F 80r, 1st line, word περιτμηθηναι) is used as well.The scribe also uses a ligature for ην not reported in F/G (at F 81v, 2nd line, last word).Text-critically, minuscule 1959 seems to be an interesting MS. In many instances (apart from spelling mistakes / variations) the text diverges from the base text I was collating against. I noticed some instances where this MS follows the Alexandrian reading over against the Majority reading (e.g. 1:18 κηφαν for πετρον; 2:14 κηφα for πετρω and πως for τι; 2:16 (second) οτι for διοτι). In 4:21 it follows the ‘Western text’ over against the Alexandrian/Majority text, in reading αναγινωσκετε for ακουετε.Finally, concerning my transcription: I am uncertain about the way I recorded what is going at the end of the 2nd line from bottom on F 84r.
